Ananya's draft conclusion states that purchasing controls at the main plant are effective, rates them satisfactory on the function's scale, and notes that the two smaller plants were outside the scope.

review: Compare the conclusion's wording with the approved scope
Evaluate whether effective processes are acknowledged, not only weaknesses
evidence: Draft conclusion wording with its rating and scope statement
Approved objectives and scope for the engagement
audit_focus.recommend: Have the engagement supervisor require the audit team to check each conclusion against the objectives, scope and rating scale.
audit_focus.decides: The chief audit executive approves the final communication that contains the conclusion

subtopics.isaca_rule: Say whether it works, within what you tested. Must: summarize results against the engagement's and management's objectives, and for assurance judge how effective governance, risk management and control are, saying so when they work (Standard 14.5). A list of findings is not a conclusion.

exam_traps.trap: When an assurance engagement produces no findings, the conclusion can be left out.
exam_traps.why: Must: an assurance conclusion includes the judgment on effectiveness and acknowledges when processes are effective. A clean result is itself a result to state.

exam_traps.trap: A strong result at one plant supports a conclusion about the whole company.
exam_traps.why: A conclusion reaches only as far as the scope and the evidence. Untested plants, periods or units are outside what the auditor can conclude on.

key_terms.definition: A set of levels, such as satisfactory through unsatisfactory, used to express conclusions consistently.
The goals the activity's management set for it, against which the engagement results are summarized.

key_terminologies.Engagement supervisor: The internal auditor who supervises an engagement: the chief audit executive, or a delegate for whom the chief audit executive stays accountable.
key_terminologies.Workpapers: The engagement's documented record of the planning, tests and evidence behind its results, kept to the function's methodology.
key_terminologies.Relevant information: Information that bears on the engagement objectives, sits inside the scope and helps build the results.
key_terminologies.Reliable information: Information that is factual and current and can be trusted, given its source and corroboration.
key_terminologies.Sufficient information: Enough trustworthy information for a capable reviewer to redo the work and reach the same conclusions.
key_terminologies.Corroboration: Confirming information against a second, separate source.
key_terminologies.Professional skepticism: An unbiased, questioning attitude: critically assessing whether information is reliable before relying on it.
key_terminologies.Walk-through: Following one transaction from start to finish to see how the process really works.
key_terminologies.Population: Every item in the set an auditor's conclusion covers, such as all payments made in a year.
key_terminologies.Structured data: Data held in fixed fields, rows and columns, such as a payments table.
key_terminologies.Unstructured data: Data with no fixed format, such as emails, contracts or call notes.
key_terminologies.Normalize: To clean and standardize data so that records from different sources can be compared.
key_terminologies.Continuous auditing: Internal audit's ongoing, technology-enabled assessment of risks and controls.
key_terminologies.Responsibility assignment matrix (RACI): A grid of tasks against roles showing who is responsible, accountable, consulted or informed for each.
key_terminologies.Analytical review: Comparing figures with expectations, through ratios, trends, variances or benchmarks, to find what needs closer testing.
key_terminologies.Benchmarking: Comparing an activity's performance with other units or sites inside the organization (internal) or with similar organizations and recognized good practice (external).
key_terminologies.Condition: What the internal auditors actually found: the existing state of the activity.
key_terminologies.Evaluation criteria: The yardsticks of what should be, such as a policy, law, contract or target.
key_terminologies.Finding: A gap between what the internal auditors found (the condition) and what should be there (the criteria).
key_terminologies.Root cause: The deeper reason a gap exists, as opposed to its visible symptom.
key_terminologies.Significance: How much a matter counts in its setting, weighing size as well as nature.
key_terminologies.Engagement conclusion: The auditor's overall judgment of what the findings, weighed together, say about the activity, stated as satisfactory or not.
key_terminologies.Retention: How long a record is kept before it is disposed of, as law and policy set.
